content:
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Cloud Infrastructure / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of experience building and operating production infrastructure, including the last 6 years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, AWS, system reliability and infrastructure design. Leads technical work across platform and product teams, turning infrastructure needs into secure, observable and maintainable services. Delivered self-service cloud infrastructure that reduced new-service delivery time from around two weeks to under one day.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment operation, Kubernetes
Infrastructure as code and delivery: Terraform, Atlantis, Argo CD, Crossplane, Helm, Kustomize, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: SLOs and error budgets, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, incident management, k6
Systems and automation: Linux, Go, Python, Bash, Puppet

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Technical lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform across 8 clusters and 3 regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Adopted by all 14 product teams; reduced new-service delivery to production from around two weeks to under one day.
- Led the move from cluster-autoscaler managed node groups to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless workloads with interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).
- Introduced SLOs, error budgets and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services, agreeing the error-budget policy with product leadership. Reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%.
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.
- Mentored three engineers transitioning into SRE from backend engineering.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure in Terraform, with approximately 40 modules, and used Atlantis to run plan/apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Ran k6 load tests and led launch capacity planning. A test simulating 300,000 concurrent players identified a connection-pool limit that was fixed before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and participated in on-call customer incident response.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes cleanup operator | Open source side project | 2024
- Built a small Kubernetes controller in Go using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

SPEAKING
UK DevOps meetup, 2024 | “SLOs that product managers care about”

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. The summary is focused, the experience bullets use credible scale and measurable outcomes, and the document demonstrates substantial AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, reliability, and developer-platform experience. The strongest evidence includes operating 8 EKS clusters across 3 regions, supporting approximately 350 services, adoption by all 14 product teams, a 38% reduction in EC2 spend, and a 60% reduction in on-call pages. The selected project and speaking sections add useful evidence of technical depth and communication. One minor professionalism issue is the present-tense wording "Participate in the incident commander rotation" within an otherwise past-tense/current-role bullet set.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, plain text, readable chronology, standard job titles, and strong keyword coverage for AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, infrastructure as code, observability, incident management, and system reliability. It should parse reliably and has a strong AI-screening probability for AWS platform, SRE, and Kubernetes infrastructure roles. Screening strength will be lower for this particular vacancy because the document does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, or explicit system-design terminology. Those are candidate-evidence gaps rather than formatting defects, so they should not be added without supporting experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform, platform design, reliability, Linux, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, analytical problem-solving, and clear technical communication. The internal developer platform, SLO programme, product-leadership collaboration, mentoring, technical lead responsibility, and load-testing example fit Corvale's engineering-led, ownership-oriented and collaborative culture. The CV also shows relevant backend-adjacent experience through game-backend infrastructure and Go/Python service templates. The main candidate-to-role gaps are Terragrunt, train/vehicle/IoT or remote-device integration, and explicit mTLS/SSL/TLS and certificate-management experience. JVM experience is also not shown. These are gaps in the candidate evidence, not defects that can be corrected through wording alone.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience section under Tallybrook Ltd, change "Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process" to "Participate in the incident commander rotation and maintain the incident and post-mortem process" if this remains an ongoing responsibility, or to "Participated in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process" if describing completed work. This removes the tense inconsistency and improves grammatical precision.
2. In the Professional Summary, change "Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, AWS, system reliability and infrastructure design" to "Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, AWS, system reliability, systems architecture and infrastructure design." This uses the job advertisement's systems-architecture terminology while remaining supported by the documented design and build work for the internal developer platform.
3. In the Core Skills section, change "Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment operation, Kubernetes" to "Cloud infrastructure and networking: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment design and operation, Kubernetes." This surfaces the job's supported terms without claiming unsupported mTLS or SSL/TLS experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "turning infrastructure needs into secure, observable and maintainable services" — the candidate's material supports observability and maintainability work, but does not specifically substantiate delivering secure services.
unsupported_claims: "turning infrastructure needs into secure, observable and maintainable services" — the candidate's material supports observability and maintainability work, but does not specifically substantiate delivering secure services.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. The summary is concise and relevant, while the experience section uses credible scale and outcome metrics: 8 clusters, 350 services, 14 product teams, 38% lower EC2 spend, and 60% fewer on-call pages. The internal developer platform, reliability programme, incident management, mentoring, and open-source project demonstrate both technical depth and leadership. The document is professional and complete for a senior infrastructure role. The main content limitation is that several role requirements—particularly Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, and explicit security practices—are not evidenced, but these are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is very good. The document uses conventional headings, reverse-chronological experience, standard text formatting, searchable technology names, and measurable achievements. Keywords such as AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, Terraform, systems architecture, infrastructure design, observability, SLOs, incident management, Go, Python, Linux, EC2, VPC and IAM are easy for an ATS to parse. AI screening probability is strong for AWS platform/SRE roles because the CV clearly shows seniority, production scale, technical leadership, Terraform, Kubernetes, reliability and cost optimisation. Screening probability will be lower for this particular role because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mutual TLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT/remote-device integration, or JVM terminology. Those should not be added without supporting experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Kubernetes platform ownership, Terraform, Linux, reliability, systems-level troubleshooting, technical leadership and measurable delivery outcomes. It also supports the company's ownership-oriented and engineering-led culture through platform ownership, self-service enablement, mentoring, incident leadership and collaboration with product leadership. The candidate's experience with service templates and supporting product teams is relevant to helping backend developers deploy services that are easy to monitor and operate. The material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, explicit secure train-to-cloud communication, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM/backend development. These are genuine alignment gaps, not CV defects. Virtual-machine experience is indirectly supported through EC2, but not described explicitly.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Professional Experience section under “Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd,” change “Participate in the incident commander rotation and maintain the incident and post-mortem process” to “Serve in the incident commander rotation and maintain the incident and post-mortem process.” This uses stronger, more ATS-readable wording without changing the claim.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Professional Summary, retain the existing quantified platform result but make the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence more explicit. For example, change the final two sentences to: “Leads technical work across platform and product teams, including agreeing error-budget policy with product leadership. Delivered self-service cloud infrastructure adopted by all 14 product teams, reducing new-service delivery time from around two weeks to under one day.” Both claims are supported by the candidate information and align more directly with the requirement to lead technical topics and bring stakeholders along.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the Core Skills section, change “Cloud infrastructure and networking” to “Cloud infrastructure, networking and environment operation.” Keep the existing AWS services and Kubernetes terms unchanged. This makes the job-description wording more directly searchable without adding unsupported networking protocols or security claims.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, achievement-focused CV with clear progression from Site Reliability Engineer to Senior Platform Engineer. The strongest content is the quantified impact: adoption by all 14 product teams, service delivery reduced from approximately two weeks to under one day, EC2 spend reduced by 38%/approximately £410,000 annually, and on-call pages reduced by approximately 60%. The document also demonstrates technical leadership, production AWS/EKS ownership, platform engineering, reliability, observability, and incident management. Structure and tone are professional, and removing the earlier Linux Systems Engineer role does not create a major content defect because Linux remains listed in Core Skills and the document stays focused on the target role. A small weakness is that several relevant capabilities are asserted in the summary or skills section without as much direct evidence in the experience bullets, particularly networking, security awareness, and system design. These are also areas where the candidate's supplied material does not provide supporting evidence, so they should not be added as claims.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience formatting, readable text, and no tables, columns, graphics, headers/footers, or unusual symbols that would interfere with parsing. It contains strong matches for AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, infrastructure as code, systems architecture, observability, SLOs, incident management, Go, Python, Linux, and technical leadership. AI screening probability is high for the core AWS/platform/SRE requirements. Screening may be weaker for exact terms such as Terragrunt, mutual TLS/mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, practical security, and IoT or remote-device integration because neither the CV nor the original candidate information supports those areas. Do not add those keywords merely to improve ATS matching. The current grouped skills format is parseable, although separating individual skills with consistent commas or bullets would make extraction slightly more reliable.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the core infrastructure and platform aspects of the role. It shows hands-on cloud infrastructure engineering and AWS environment design and operation through production EKS ownership, multi-region operation, Terraform, Crossplane, Karpenter, and self-service infrastructure. It shows systems and platform design through the internal developer platform, service templates, GitOps, and self-service provisioning. Technical leadership and stakeholder engagement are supported by the platform-team lead role, agreement of the error-budget policy with product leadership, mentoring, and participation in incident leadership. Analytical thinking and communication are supported by capacity planning, k6 testing, identifying a connection-pool limit before launch, quantified reliability improvements, and the meetup speaking entry. The candidate's material does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, certificate management, practical security work, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, JVM experience, or virtual-machine experience; these are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be fixed through rewriting. Linux is shown, but virtual machines are not.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the strongest role-relevant evidence more explicit by changing the final two sentences to: "Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, AWS cloud environment design and operation, Kubernetes platforms, systems architecture, and infrastructure design. Leads technical work across platform and product teams, including self-service cloud infrastructure that reduced new-service delivery from around two weeks to under one day." This keeps the ad's terminology while tying it directly to evidence already present in the CV.
2. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience section, revise the internal developer platform bullet so the design and stakeholder impact are even clearer: "Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3; adopted by all 14 product teams and reduced new-service delivery to production from around two weeks to under one day." 
3. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience section, revise the SLO bullet to foreground stakeholder alignment and communication: "Introduced SLOs, error budgets and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services, agreeing the error-budget policy with product leadership; reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%." This is already substantively present, but the semicolon structure improves scanability and makes the stakeholder requirement easier to identify.
4. In Core Skills, use consistent comma-separated skill items within each category rather than mixing broad phrases and tool lists. For example, retain the existing categories but format them as: "Cloud infrastructure and networking: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Kubernetes, cloud environment design and operation" and similarly keep each tool as a distinct parseable item. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, security, IoT, JVM, or virtual machines because the original candidate information does not support them.
